Description / Purpose: Analyzing crystal (monochromator) used on each spectrometer assignment. Crystal choice determines the detectable wavelength range and dispersion.
Example / Allowed Content: LIF | LLIF | LIFL | LIFH | PET | LPET | PETL | PETH | PETJ | TAP | TAPL | TAPH | LTAP | LDE1 | LDE2 | LDE3 | RAP | KAP | ADP | Other: specify | Unknown | N/A | None

Description / Purpose: WDS spectrometer position(s) assigned to each analyte, one entry per assignment. An analyte may be assigned to more than one spectrometer with intensities aggregated (aggregate intensity counting), and one spectrometer serves several analytes across a run, so the assignment — not the analyte — is the unit carrying the spectrometer setup. Different spectrometers may have different crystal configurations.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., 'Si=Sp1; Ti=Sp2; Cr=Sp2+Sp3 (aggregate intensity counting); Fe=Sp3' | 'Mg=Sp1; Ca=Sp4; Na=Sp5'

Description / Purpose: Number, type, and crystal range of WDS spectrometers on the instrument. Include manufacturer, model, and crystal range. For SEM-WDS configurations (third-party WDS on a non-EPMA platform), include WDS manufacturer and model.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., '5 Rowland-circle WDS spectrometers (JEOL), crystal range LDE1-LIFH' | '4 WDS spectrometers (Cameca)'

Description / Purpose: Method used to correct for WDS proportional counter dead time at high count rates. Dead time errors are most significant for major elements with high count rates (e.g., Si, Fe, Ca). Unlike EDS dead time — which is hardware-managed and reported as a session QC percentage (see EDS Dead Time) — WDS dead time correction is a user-selectable algorithm in the data reduction software. No separate measured WDS dead time value is reported; the correction is applied transparently during intensity-to-concentration conversion.
Example / Allowed Content: Default constant 3 us (Cameca) | Adjusted constant (Cameca) | Default constant (JEOL) | Adjusted constant (JEOL) | High-precision (Probe for EPMA) | Logarithmic | Super-precision | Other: specify | Unknown | N/A | None

Description / Purpose: Pulse height analyzer (PHA) setting for the WDS detector. Integral mode accepts all pulses above a threshold; Differential mode selects a narrow energy window to reject higher-order reflections and escape peaks.
Example / Allowed Content: Integral | Differential | Other: specify | Unknown | N/A | None

Description / Purpose: X-ray emission line measured on each spectrometer assignment. Line choice affects sensitivity, matrix correction accuracy, and susceptibility to peak overlap and spectral interference.
Example / Allowed Content: Ka | Kb | La | Lb | Lg | Ma | Mb | Other: specify | N/A | None

Description / Purpose: Time spent counting X-ray intensity at the peak position, in seconds, on each spectrometer assignment. Procedure specifies standard values; analysts may adjust within procedure-defined bounds.
Total time spent counting at off-peak background position(s) in seconds, summed across all background positions.
Location(s) of off-peak background measurement(s) relative to the peak, in mm or sin-theta, and whether on the high- or low-energy side.
Example / Allowed Content: e.g., '+5 mm (High), -5 mm (Low)' | 'High only (+4 mm)' | 'MAN method (no off-peak positions)'

Description / Purpose: Type of detector used on each spectrometer assignment. Affects sensitivity and count rate linearity.
Example / Allowed Content: High Pressure P10 Flow | Low Pressure P10 Flow | Xe Sealed | SDD | Si(Li) | Other: specify | Unknown | N/A | None

Description / Purpose: Percent dead time reported by the EDS detector during the session — the fraction of total acquisition time the detector spent processing rather than counting. EDS dead time correction is managed automatically by the detector electronics; this field documents the resulting percentage as a session QC metric. Values above ~40% indicate excessive count rate and may degrade spectral quality and quantitative accuracy. Unlike WDS dead time (see WDS Dead Time Correction), no user-selectable correction algorithm is required.

Description / Purpose: Method used to process EDS spectra and extract net peak intensities from raw spectral data. Applied before quantification (see Matrix Correction Method). Common approaches include background fitting and subtraction followed by peak integration, and filter fit or Gaussian deconvolution for overlapping peaks.
Example / Allowed Content: Background fitting | Peak deconvolution | Top-hat filter | Gaussian fit | Filter fit | Other: specify | Unknown | N/A | None

Description / Purpose: Number of pixels in the EDS map in the X and Y directions. Determined at analysis time based on the area of interest and selected pixel size.

Order in which spectrometer assignments are acquired during point analysis. Relevant for minimizing beam damage (volatile elements measured first) and for sequential multi-channel setups. Not applicable to X-ray mapping, where all assigned spectrometers collect simultaneously at each pixel.
